receipt.public_excerpt: Experiments reveal leading LLM agents achieve only around 58% single-turn success on CRMArena-Pro, with performance dropping significantly to approximately 35% in multi-turn settings.

evidence_items.explanation: Leading agents failed about two-thirds of realistic multi-turn business tasks. That supports the contextual claim that agents do not work as dependable autonomous workers.

receipt.public_excerpt: find that the most competitive agent can complete 30% of tasks autonomously. This paints a nuanced picture on task automation with LM agents--in a setting simulating a real workplace, a good portion of simpler tasks could be solved autonomously, but more difficult long-horizon tasks are still beyond the reach of current systems.

evidence_items.explanation: An independent workplace benchmark found the best agent completed 30% of tasks autonomously, with long-horizon tasks out of reach. This fits the contextual reading. It is context only because this abstract version is dated after the post.

receipt.public_excerpt: On these tasks, current frontier AI models such as Claude 3.7 Sonnet have a 50% time horizon of around 50 minutes.

evidence_items.explanation: Frontier agents could complete roughly hour-long software tasks about half the time. This shows real but unreliable bounded capability. It would contradict a literal zero-capability reading, but not the contextual reading.

unresolved_gaps: Benchmarks may not capture all real-world deployments where agents are used under human supervision.
No standard reliability threshold defines when an agent 'works'.
